summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis report (N27) evaluating whether rolipram retains residual working-memory / object-recognition / LTP-linked cognitive phenotype (≥50% of rolipram-alone) under conditions that abolish PDE4-class attribution via Pde4b/Pde4d genetic LOF or PDE4-matched blockade. The document synthesizes four key literature priors (Barad, Zhang HT, Rutten, Li) and concludes that no published head-to-head study scores residual-positive rolipram cognition under PDE4 abolish; the Li (2011) occlusion study is explicitly AGAINST residual. The hypothesis is labeled NEGATIVE/assumption-kill with execution status NOT_RUN.

content_blocks.title: Hypothesis Overview and Claim (N27)
content_blocks.content: N27 asks whether residual rolipram working-memory / object-recognition / LTP-linked cognitive phenotype survives Pde4b/Pde4d genetic LOF or PDE4-matched blockade that abolishes PDE4-class attribution on the same panel (Barad/Zhang HT/Rutten/Li-class). The pre-registered claim: under the abolish condition, rolipram retains residual WM/cognitive phenotype ≥50% of rolipram-alone (WM/object-recognition/cognition units as pre-specified; α/N pre-specified). This is framed as an 'assumption-kill / pde4-insufficiency' test. Status: NEGATIVE, execution_status=NOT_RUN.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art Summary — Four Key Literature Priors
content_blocks.content:
Four published studies are cited as the evidence base:

1. Barad (PMID 9844008, PNAS 1998): Rolipram facilitates late-LTP (CA1 after single tetanus) and improves long-term contextual freezing in young/aged mice. LTP/memory phenotype prior; WT PDE4 present; NO PDE4-abolish residual arm.

2. Zhang HT (PMID 10923759, Psychopharmacology 2000): Rolipram reverses scopolamine-induced working and reference memory errors in rat radial-arm maze. WM phenotype prior; WT PDE4 present; NO PDE4-abolish residual arm.

3. Rutten (PMID 16242977, Neurobiol Learn Mem 2006): Rolipram reverses scopolamine- and time-dependent object-recognition deficits. OR phenotype prior; WT PDE4 present; NO PDE4-abolish residual arm.

4. Li (PMID 21209202, J Neurosci 2011): PDE4D KO / RNAi enhance memory (radial-arm, water maze, object recognition) and hippocampal neurogenesis; mimicked by rolipram in WT (phenocopy). CRITICAL: rolipram WAS tested IN 4DKO — memory enhancement in 4DKO not affected by chronic rolipram; rolipram did not alter memory in PDE4D-deficient mice — cogn occlusion / necessity AGAINST residual.

content_blocks.title: Promoted (Out-of-Public) Prior Art
content_blocks.content:
Two additional studies are noted as 'promoted; OUT of public prior_art':

- Zhang (PMID 12377395, Neuropsychopharmacology 2002): Rolipram produces antidepressant-like TST/FST effects only in PDE4D+/+ mice. Antidepressant necessity AGAINST residual for that endpoint; explicitly NOT a cognitive WM/OR residual H2H.

- Wang (PMID 23003922, Br J Pharmacol 2013): Mouse PFC long-form PDE4D-shRNA ± rolipram; TST/FST / NOR / MWM. PDE4D-shRNA cogn/antidep effects not enhanced by rolipram — adjacent occlusion AGAINST residual misread; not residual-positive H2H.

content_blocks.title: Prediction Variables and Assay Design
content_blocks.content:
Key prediction variables defined in the document:

1. Barad_rolipram_late_LTP_memory_phenotype [LITERATURE]: Mouse hippocampal slices (CA1 late-LTP after single tetanus) + young/aged mice contextual freezing ± rolipram. Threshold: rolipram facilitates late-LTP and improves long-term contextual freezing. No PDE4-abolish residual arm.

2. Zhang_HT_rolipram_radial_arm_WM_phenotype [LITERATURE]: Rat eight-arm radial maze WM/reference errors ± scopolamine ± rolipram. Threshold: rolipram reverses scopolamine-induced WM and reference memory errors. No PDE4-abolish residual arm.

3. Rutten_rolipram_object_recognition_phenotype [LITERATURE]: Rat object recognition ± delay ± scopolamine ± rolipram. Threshold: rolipram reverses scopolamine- and time-dependent object-recognition deficits. No PDE4-abolish residual arm.

4. Li_PDE4D_KO_phenocopy_cogn_occlusion_not_residual [LITERATURE]: PDE4D KO (4DKO) vs WT ± chronic rolipram; radial-arm / water maze / object recognition. Result: PDE4D KO enhances memory (phenocopy of rolipram-in-WT); rolipram in 4DKO — no further memory enhance; AGAINST residual.

5. matched_residual_rolipram_under_PDE4_abolish_of_PDE4_class_attribution_H2H [UNKNOWN]: Same acute/subacute rodent WM/OR/LTP-linked cognition panel — rolipram ± Pde4b/Pde4d LOF or PDE4-matched abolish condition. Result: dedicated residual-positive rolipram under PDE4 abolish NOT FOUND as residual-positive (soft-complete Q_resid_tight=1 REVIEW NON-MATCH).

6. residual_rolipram_phenotype_ge_50pct_of_alone_when_PDE4_class_abolished [PREDICTION]: Pre-registered panel; PDE4-class arm must show abolished attribution; rolipram arm scored for residual phenotype vs rolipram-alone. Threshold: ≥50% of rolipram-alone in WM/OR/cognition units; α/N pre-specified.

7. competing_abolish_fail_or_rolipram_null_or_underpowered_inconclusive [PREDICTION]: Competing outcomes if abolish condition fails to kill PDE4-class attribution, rolipram-alone null, underpowered strata, or assay-identity mismatch.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism and Experimental Strategy
content_blocks.content:
Mechanism: Rolipram is a selective PDE4 inhibitor; its WM/OR/LTP-linked cognitive phenotypes are framed as PDE4 orthosteric blockade. Pde4d KO (Li) serves as genetic tool. The test asks whether PDE4-class sufficiency for the rolipram phenotype holds (i.e., does rolipram retain ≥50% of its cognitive effect when PDE4 is genetically or pharmacologically abolished?).

Preferred execution path: cell/slice/block-QC before new animal (e.g., hippocampal-slice LTP Barad-class or PDE4 activity QC for abolish gate); in vivo Barad/Zhang HT/Rutten/Li-class rodent WM/OR/cognition panel as primary kill path.

Key distinctions: N27 is explicitly NOT equivalent to N15 (DAT≠PDE4), N22 (AMPT≠PDE4 LOF), N23 (α2≠PDE4), N24 (A2A≠PDE4), N25 (NET≠PDE4; atomoxetine≠rolipram), N26 (SERT≠PDE4; fluoxetine≠rolipram).

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria and Competing Caveats
content_blocks.content:
Refute if: On the pre-registered acute/subacute rodent panel, under Pde4b/Pde4d LOF or PDE4-matched blockade that abolishes PDE4-class attribution, residual rolipram WM/cognitive phenotype falls below 50% of rolipram-alone — so PDE4-class sufficiency for the rolipram phenotype survives and pde4-insufficiency fails — when abolish-gate, rolipram-alone comparator, and power/assay artifacts are ruled out.

Competing caveats (inconclusive rather than refuted): abolish condition fails to kill PDE4-class attribution; rolipram-alone null; underpowered strata; assay-identity mismatch (phenotype≠residual; phenocopy≠residual-under-abolish; antidepressant TST/FST≠cogn panel; occlusion≠residual-positive).

key_findings: No published head-to-head study scores residual-positive rolipram WM/cognitive phenotype under PDE4 abolish (Pde4b/Pde4d LOF or PDE4-matched blockade) on the same panel — PRIOR_ART PARTIAL.

Li (PMID 21209202, J Neurosci 2011): Rolipram was tested IN PDE4D KO (4DKO) mice — no further memory enhancement observed; rolipram did not alter memory in PDE4D-deficient mice — cogn occlusion AGAINST residual-positive interpretation.
Barad (PMID 9844008), Zhang HT (PMID 10923759), and Rutten (PMID 16242977) are phenotype priors only (WT PDE4 present); none include a PDE4-abolish residual arm.

Zhang (PMID 12377395, promoted/out-of-public): Rolipram antidepressant TST/FST effects only in PDE4D+/+ — antidepressant necessity AGAINST residual for that endpoint; not a cognitive WM/OR residual H2H.
Wang (PMID 23003922, promoted/out-of-public): PDE4D-shRNA cognitive/antidepressant effects not enhanced by rolipram — adjacent occlusion AGAINST residual misread.
The matched residual-positive rolipram under Pde4b/Pde4d LOF or PDE4-matched blockade that abolishes PDE4-class attribution is UNKNOWN as residual-positive; execution_status=NOT_RUN.
Hypothesis is labeled NEGATIVE (assumption-kill); kill_cost_tier=1; time_to_refute=4 weeks; ip_class=pde4-insufficiency.

Preferred experimental path: cell/slice/block-QC (hippocampal-slice LTP or PDE4 activity QC) before new animal; in vivo Barad/Zhang HT/Rutten/Li-class rodent WM/OR/cognition panel as primary kill path.

Refutation threshold: residual rolipram WM/cognitive phenotype <50% of rolipram-alone under verified PDE4-class abolish condition (with abolish-gate, rolipram-alone comparator, and power/assay artifacts ruled out).
N27 is explicitly distinct from N15–N26 (DAT≠PDE4, SERT≠PDE4, NET≠PDE4, A2A≠PDE4, α2≠PDE4, AMPT≠PDE4 LOF); N1–N26 do not prove N27.
